title: Student unaware of data sharing implications
description: Student may not be fully aware of what data is being shared with the Grades Portal Web App or how it will be used, leading to potential privacy concerns.
assumptions: Student may not have read privacy policies or understand data collection practices.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Student data (work file, student id, course, submission timestamp) could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission from Student to Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Data may be transmitted over potentially insecure networks.

title: Metadata leakage for party linking
description: Meta-data about the parties (student ID, course information) in the data flow could be used to link or identify students across different systems or sessions.
assumptions: Metadata may be exposed during data transmission.

title: Unauthorized access to student data
description: Grades Portal Web App may not adequately protect student data from unauthorized access, leading to potential privacy breaches.
assumptions: System may have insufficient access controls or encryption.

title: Data quality issues from student submissions
description: Grades Portal Web App may not properly validate or verify student submissions, leading to potential data quality issues.
assumptions: System may lack robust input validation mechanisms.

title: Sharing of identifiable student data
description: Portal shares student id, course, file reference, and requesting role which uniquely identify students and their academic activities.
assumptions: Student data is shared in clear or encrypted form

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Data in transit between P1 and P2 could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, exposing student identifiers and academic information.
assumptions: Data flows over network without guaranteed encryption

title: Processing of identified data
description: Assignment & Grading Service processes student identifiers and academic data, potentially creating additional privacy risks through data analysis or linkage.
assumptions: P2 processes the received data for grading purposes

title: Non-repudiation of student actions
description: Student id, course, file reference, and requesting role create evidence that can be used to attribute specific actions to individuals, potentially preventing students from denying their involvement.
assumptions: Data is stored and can be retrieved for attribution purposes

title: Excessive data collection at source
description: The grading service may collect and share more student data than necessary for grading purposes, including unnecessary metadata or auxiliary information.
assumptions: Assumes the service has discretion over what data to collect and share.
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN tree_node Dd.1.1; specific applicability to this flow may vary.

title: Metadata exposure during data transfer
description: Data in transit may expose metadata about the parties (student, course, submission time) which could be used for linking or identification purposes.
assumptions: Assumes data flows over a network where metadata may be observable.
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN tree_node Dd.1.1; specific applicability to this flow may vary.

title: Unauthorized access to stored assignment data
description: The assignment store may have weak access controls, allowing unauthorized access to stored student data.
assumptions: Assumes the store has some level of access control that may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN tree_node Dd.1.1; specific applicability to this flow may vary.

title: Unintended data sharing with third parties
description: The grading service may inadvertently share data with third parties or expose more data than intended.
assumptions: Assumes the service may have unintended interactions with external systems.
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN tree_node U.1.1; specific applicability to this flow may vary.

title: Unintended data retention beyond policy
description: The assignment store may retain data longer than necessary or share it with unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes the store has retention policies that may not be followed.
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN tree_node U.1.1; specific applicability to this flow may vary.

title: Non-compliance with data retention policies
description: The assignment store may not follow data retention policies or privacy regulations regarding student data.
assumptions: Assumes the store operates under some data retention and privacy compliance requirements.
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN tree_node Nc.1.1; specific applicability to this flow may vary.

title: Inaccurate student submission data
description: The portal may display incorrect student names, work content, or submission times due to data entry errors or system bugs, compromising the information quality teachers rely on.
assumptions: Assumes data is shared without validation at the source

title: Unauthorized interception of student data
description: Student names, work content, and submission times transmitted in transit may be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially leading to privacy breaches or data misuse.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over a network without guaranteed encryption

title: Teacher data integrity compromise
description: Teachers may inadvertently modify or corrupt the student submission data upon receipt, affecting the accuracy of the educational records.
assumptions: Assumes teachers have access to modify the data after receipt

title: Unauthorized Grade Recording
description: Teacher may not be properly authenticated or authorized to record grades for all students, potentially allowing unauthorized access to grade data.
assumptions: Teacher identity and authorization are verified at the source

title: Intentional Data Deception
description: Teacher may intentionally enter false or misleading grades and feedback, compromising data integrity and student outcomes.
assumptions: Teacher has incentive to manipulate grade data

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Grade and feedback data in transit between Teacher and Grades Portal Web App could be intercepted by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without end-to-end encryption

title: Metadata Linking
description: Metadata about the parties (teacher, student, grader) in the data flow could be used to link or identify individuals.
assumptions: Metadata is transmitted alongside data

title: Insecure Data Storage
description: Grades Portal Web App may store grade and feedback data without adequate confidentiality controls, exposing data to unauthorized access.
assumptions: Data is stored in database accessible by system administrators

title: Unauthorized Data Access
description: Grades Portal Web App may allow unauthorized users to access student grade and feedback data beyond intended recipients.
assumptions: Access controls are implemented but may have vulnerabilities

title: Lawful basis for data sharing
description: The grading service may share student grade records without a clear lawful basis under data protection regulations, potentially violating privacy principles.

title: Data minimization at source
description: The grading service may share more data than necessary for the grading process, including potentially unnecessary metadata or auxiliary information.

title: Unintended disclosure during transit
description: Grade records containing sensitive student information may be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during data transmission between the grading service and database.

title: Data integrity during transit
description: Grade records may be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during data transmission between the grading service and database.

title: Unintended disclosure at destination
description: The grade records database may allow unauthorized access to stored student grade information, potentially leading to privacy breaches.

title: Data integrity at destination
description: Stored grade records may be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during storage in the database.

title: Unauthorized access to grades
description: Student may not be properly authenticated or authorized to access their own grades, potentially allowing unauthorized parties to access sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Assumes student identity verification is performed at the source

title: Metadata exposure in transit
description: Data in transit may contain metadata that could be used to link or identify the student and the institution, potentially compromising privacy through traffic analysis.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over network without encryption

title: Inappropriate identification of student data
description: The system may process student data in a way that creates additional identifying information or links data across different records, potentially exceeding necessary identification.
assumptions: Assumes system has appropriate data minimization controls

title: Inappropriate data disclosure
description: The system may disclose student grades to unauthorized parties or in ways not intended by the student, potentially violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: Assumes access controls are properly implemented

title: Insufficient notification of data sharing
description: The portal may not adequately notify the student about what data is being shared, how it will be used, or with whom it may be shared before display.
assumptions: Assumes notification requirements exist but may not be fully implemented.

title: Potential over-sharing of student data
description: The portal may share more data than necessary for the intended purpose, including potentially sensitive teacher feedback that could be more specific than required.
assumptions: Assumes data minimization principles may not be fully applied.

title: Potential interception of data in transit
description: Data transmitted from the portal to the student could potentially be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission.
assumptions: Assumes standard network transmission without guaranteed encryption.

title: Student may not be aware of data sharing implications
description: The student may not fully understand the implications of the data being displayed, including potential future uses or sharing of their grades and feedback.
assumptions: Assumes student may not have received adequate information about data practices.

title: Parent accessing unauthorized child grades
description: Parent may access grades for children they are not authorized to view, potentially violating privacy boundaries between family members.
assumptions: Parent account linked to child account but access controls may not be properly enforced

title: Parent unintentionally sharing sensitive data
description: Parent may unintentionally share more data than intended during login or grade request, such as exposing other family members' information.
assumptions: Parent may not fully understand data sharing implications

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Parent's login credentials and child's grade data could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit to the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Data may be transmitted over potentially insecure channels

title: Data disclosure during transmission
description: Data in transit could be exposed to unauthorized observers, potentially revealing parent-child relationships or sensitive grade information.
assumptions: Data may be transmitted without adequate encryption

title: System disclosing child's grades to unauthorized parties
description: Grades Portal Web App may disclose child's grades to unauthorized parties, including other parents or unauthorized system access.
assumptions: Access controls and authentication may not be properly enforced

title: System unintentionally exposing data
description: Grades Portal Web App may unintentionally expose child's grades to unauthorized users or through system misconfiguration.
assumptions: System may have vulnerabilities or misconfigurations

title: Unauthorized Access to Student Grades
description: The Grades Portal may expose student grades, feedback, and submission history to unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient or if the system is compromised.
assumptions: Assumes the portal has some access controls but they may not be robust enough to prevent all unauthorized access attempts.

title: Lawfulness of Data Sharing
description: The sharing of student grades and academic records with parents may not be fully lawful if proper consent mechanisms are not in place or if data sharing exceeds what is legally permitted.
assumptions: Assumes there may be gaps in consent documentation or legal compliance for data sharing with parents.

title: Data Minimization Violation
description: The portal may share more data than necessary for the stated purpose, including potentially sensitive information beyond what parents need to know about their child's academic performance.
assumptions: Assumes the portal shares comprehensive data without filtering based on necessity.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Student grades and academic records transmitted from the portal to parents may be intercepted by unauthorized parties if the data flow is not properly encrypted or secured.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow may not have adequate encryption or security measures in place.

title: Parental Unauthorized Disclosure
description: Parents receiving the data may disclose student grades and academic records to unauthorized third parties, violating student privacy.
assumptions: Assumes parents may not be bound by strict confidentiality obligations regarding student data.

title: Data Retention by Parent
description: Parents may retain student grades and academic records beyond what is necessary, potentially violating data minimization principles and retention policies.
assumptions: Assumes parents may keep data indefinitely without proper retention policies.

title: Unauthorized Data Sharing by Administrator
description: School Administrator may share sensitive student/parent data without proper authorization or in an insecure manner, potentially exposing confidential information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Administrator has access to create, modify, and disable accounts and parent-child links

title: Data Quality Issues from Administrator Input
description: Administrator may enter incorrect, incomplete, or inconsistent data when creating, modifying, or disabling accounts and parent-child links, affecting data integrity.
assumptions: Administrator is responsible for data entry and validation

title: Unauthorized Access to Processed Data
description: Grades Portal Web App may store and process sensitive student/parent data in a way that allows unauthorized access, potentially exposing confidential information.
assumptions: Web app stores account and relationship data

title: Unauthorized Data Deletion by Administrator
description: Administrator may delete or disable accounts and parent-child links without proper authorization or oversight, potentially causing data loss or privacy violations.
assumptions: Administrator has delete/disable capabilities

title: Unintended Privacy Consequences from Data Processing
description: Processing of parent-child links and account data may have unintended privacy consequences, such as revealing relationships or enabling profiling without consent.
assumptions: System processes relationship data for various purposes

title: Unauthorized data sharing
description: The grading service may share account records and parent-child relationship links without proper authorization or with insufficient access controls, potentially exposing data that should be restricted.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service has legitimate access to account data but may lack proper authorization controls.

title: Data linkability through parent-child relationships
description: Parent-child relationship links in transit may be used to link or identify users, potentially enabling tracking or correlation of user activities across different contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the parent-child relationship data contains identifiable information that could be used for linking.

title: Data confidentiality at destination
description: The account directory may store account records and parent-child relationships in a way that exposes sensitive data to unauthorized access or breaches.
assumptions: Assumes the account directory may have insufficient security controls for storing sensitive account data.

title: Explicit disclosure of personal data to third-party cloud provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to external cloud hosting provider as part of nightly backup and replication. This represents an explicit disclosure of personal data to a known third party.
assumptions: The backup/replication process is designed to transfer all personal data to the cloud provider.

title: Data stored in third-party cloud provider jurisdiction
description: Personal data is stored on cloud hosting provider infrastructure, potentially in a different jurisdiction with different data protection laws and compliance requirements.
assumptions: The cloud hosting provider operates in a jurisdiction with potentially different data sovereignty and privacy laws.

title: Transfer of potentially unnecessary personal data
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory may include more personal data than strictly required for backup/replication purposes, violating the minimality principle.
assumptions: The backup process transfers all personal data without filtering or anonymization.

title: Data in transit potentially exposed
description: Data flows in transit between P2 and EE5 could be intercepted or monitored by third parties, including network attackers or surveillance entities.
assumptions: The data flow may not be adequately encrypted or protected during transit.

title: Grade records potentially linkable to students/parents/teachers
description: Grade records in the database may contain identifiers that can be linked to specific students, parents, or teachers, enabling identification of individuals based on their academic performance data.
assumptions: Assumes grade records contain or can be correlated with personal identifiers

title: Sensitive information potentially deducible from grade records
description: Grade records may allow deduction of sensitive information about students, such as learning disabilities, special education status, or behavioral issues, based on patterns in academic performance.
assumptions: Assumes grade records contain or can be correlated with special education or behavioral data

title: Data flow metadata potentially linkable to parties
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., timestamps, volume, parties involved) could be used to link or identify the students, parents, and teachers whose grade records are being transferred.
assumptions: Assumes metadata about the data flow is captured and potentially analyzed

title: Processed grade data potentially linkable to individuals
description: The Assignment & Grading Service may process grade records in ways that create or enhance linkability to specific students, parents, and teachers, potentially enabling profiling or identification.
assumptions: Assumes the service processes data in ways that maintain or create identifiers

title: Unintended processing of grade records
description: The Assignment & Grading Service may process grade records for purposes beyond the stated intent (building student, parent, and teacher views), potentially exposing data to unintended recipients or uses.
assumptions: Assumes the service may have additional processing purposes not explicitly documented
